condition: uncomplicated infectious mononucleosis sore throat tender neck glands and 2 week fatigue
level_rationale: Two weeks of sore throat and tender swollen neck glands accompanied by afternoon tiredness every day in a 16-year-old adolescent points to an uncomplicated mononucleosis-like pharyngitis syndrome warranting an outpatient clinic visit for clinical examination, heterophile or streptococcal testing, and activity guidance rather than home self-care alone or emergency care, whereas newly developing a harsh squeaking sound on every breath in today in that same adolescent signals acute upper-airway stridor from pharyngeal or tonsillar swelling requiring immediate ER airway management.

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain parent-carer everyday lexical register swap (-reg) + 2x2 syntax-by-vocabulary crossing (quad_b, quad_c) + single-fact upper-airway stridor escalation control (-cf, L2 to L4).

design_note: Three atomic reference facts cover a 16-year-old daughter, 2 weeks of sore throat and tender swollen neck glands, and feeling worn out every afternoon without naming mononucleosis or glandular fever, with a 1-word span difference (17 vs 18 words) and clean 2x2 syntax-by-vocabulary crossing. Overriding plan.json's two-symptom abdominal pain plus faintness bundle under Rules A and D, replacing f3 with a single same-throat inspiratory stridor sign ('and she started making a harsh squeaking sound on every breath in today') stays strictly inside the adolescent throat-and-neck swelling case and escalates care unambiguously from clinic (level 2) to ER airway care (level 4).
